    One-middle algebra meshes as literal unary boundaries #

    Coefficient duality turns the selected right almost-split map at an algebra skeleton object into a left almost-split monomorphism. Rotating across its cokernel produces a literal right almost-split problem. When the original mesh has one middle occurrence, literal boundary classification gives a unary boundary, while uniqueness of kernels identifies its kernel word with the coefficient dual of the original endpoint.
